title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 31
paragraphs: From Phrygia he entered Lydia, and here the road forks: the one going left leads to Caria, the one going right to Sardis. Taking this latter road, one must cross the Maeander and pass the city of Callatebus, where men make their living by producing a honey from tamarisk and wheat flour. Xerxes went by this road and found a plane-tree, to which, for its beauty, he gave an adornment of gold and appointed a keeper for it in perpetual succession. On the next day he came to the city of the Lydians.
